name: Maaziah
overview: Maaziah was a male Levite who served as the twenty-fourth chosen priest among the twenty-four priestly courses established for temple service. He belonged to the line of Ithamar, one of the two sons of Aaron through whom the priestly lineage continued. His role as a priest placed him in the sacred duties of worship and temple ministry during the time of the divided priestly courses.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaziah means 'YHWH is a refuge,' reflecting a trust in God's protection and care. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 24:18, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful theophoric element common in Hebrew names.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Maaziah as a descendant of Ithamar, situating him within the priestly family line descending from Aaron's son. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded for Maaziah in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Maaziah's significance lies in his inclusion among the twenty-four priestly courses that organized the Levitical service in the temple, a system that ensured orderly worship and sacrifice. Being from the line of Ithamar highlights the continuation of priestly duties through Aaron's descendants. His role underscores the biblical emphasis on divinely appointed ministry and the faithful administration of temple worship.
